summary: Add customer_note column via the new version's Django migration on deploy_new, backfill existing note values into customer_note before retiring the old version, then drop the note column. This avoids the column-already-exists conflict and ensures the note column remains the source of truth for runner checks during the overlap.
write_consistency: The old version continues writing to the note column throughout; the new version writes to customer_note. The backfill SQL stage runs after deploy_new (following the migration that adds customer_note), ensuring customer_note is populated from note. Since no SQL stages run during the overlap between deploy_new and retire_old, and the old version is the sole writer to note, the note column always reflects the most recent old-version write, satisfying the runner's column-check. After retire_old, the note column is dropped.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed because the SQL expand stage added customer_note before deploy_new, causing the new version's Django migration to fail with 'column customer_note already exists'. This revised plan lets the new version's own migration add the column during deploy_new, then performs the data backfill as a SQL stage after deploy_new. The note column is retained for the old version during the overlap and only dropped after retire_old.

stages.description: Copy every note value into customer_note after the new version's migration has added the column
Retire the old version; after this the note column is free to be contracted
